title: ChatGPT can't see your website

beats.say: If an AI tool built your website, ChatGPT probably can't read a single word of it.
Most AI-built apps draw the whole page with JavaScript, inside your visitor's browser.
But AI crawlers don't run JavaScript. Vercel tracked them across its network, and none of them render it.
So to ChatGPT, your landing page is one empty div.

vis.sub: everything GPTBot reads on your page

beats.say: And these bots are busy. GPTBot alone made five hundred and sixty nine million requests in one month on Vercel.
When someone asks AI for the best tool like yours, it recommends the sites it can actually read.

vis.title: ChatGPT
msgs: What's the best app to plan a weekend launch?
Here are 3 options: Launchly, ShipFast and Kitwise. Each has...

beats.say: The fix is server rendering. Send real HTML first, then load the JavaScript.
Here's the prompt. Screenshot it, and send it to Claude inside your project.
Follow Ship With Pip for one of these every day.

prompt: Check how my site looks to an AI crawler that doesn't run JavaScript: fetch the raw HTML of every public page. If the main text, title, meta description or links are missing, add server-side rendering or prerendering for those pages, plus a sitemap.xml and robots.txt. Show me the before and after HTML.
caption: If an AI tool built your site, ChatGPT may only see an empty <div>. Vercel's data (Dec 2024): the major AI crawlers, including GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot, don't render JavaScript, and GPTBot made 569M requests in a month on Vercel's network alone. Server-render your key pages so AI can read and recommend you. The prompt is at the end.
sources: Vercel, 'The rise of the AI crawler' (Dec 17, 2024): no major AI crawler renders JS except Gemini (Googlebot) and AppleBot; GPTBot 569M, Claude 370M fetches/month
